levels.name: A1 — Beginner
levels.description: First steps in Mandarin: greetings, numbers, basic verbs and questions.

topics.title: Greetings
topics.description: Say hello, goodbye, and how are you

guide.intro: Mandarin has only a handful of greetings to learn — but the tones really matter. Here's what to know before you start.

sections.text: The four tones

Every Mandarin syllable has one of four pitched tones (plus a neutral "fifth" tone). The same syllable means different things depending on tone — so "mā", "má", "mǎ", and "mà" are four different words.
Hello: 你好 (nǐ hǎo)
你 means "you" and 好 means "good". Put them together for "you good?" — the standard hello, usable any time of day.
When two 3rd-tone syllables stack like nǐ hǎo, the first one shifts up to a 2nd tone in speech (ní hǎo). It still gets written as nǐ hǎo.
你 (nǐ) vs 您 (nín)
您 is the polite form of "you" — used with elders, customers, and strangers. 你 is everyday/casual. Both pronounced almost the same.

rows.translation: Hi there.
Hello (formal).
Hello, teacher.

sections.text: How are you?
To turn a statement into a yes/no question, just add 嗎 (ma) at the end. So 你好 ("you're good") + 嗎 = 你好嗎? ("are you good?").

rows.translation: How are you?
I am very good.
Not bad.

lessons.title: Hello & goodbye
lessons.description: The two phrases you can't live without

exercises.prompt: What does "你好" (nǐ hǎo) mean?
How do you say "goodbye"?
"再見" (zài jiàn) means ___
exercises.explanation: "再見" literally means "see you again."

exercises.prompt: the greeting to its meaning
Tap the phrase you hear
exercises.explanation: 你好 (nǐ hǎo) is the everyday hello — both syllables third tone, but the first becomes second tone in speech.

exercises.prompt: You meet your friend's grandmother for the first time. What do you say?
exercises.explanation: 您 (nín) is the polite "you" — used with elders, customers, and strangers to show respect.

exercises.prompt: "明天見" (míng tiān jiàn) means "see you ___"
exercises.explanation: 見 (jiàn) means "see/meet" — pair it with a time word to schedule a goodbye.

exercises.prompt: Build: "Hello, Teacher!"
exercises.explanation: Putting 老師 first is a respectful way to address a teacher before the greeting.

exercises.prompt: Which is NOT a way to say goodbye?
exercises.explanation: 拜拜 (bài bài) is borrowed from English "bye-bye" and is very common in casual speech.

exercises.prompt: Tap the phrase you hear
"拜拜" (bài bài) means ___
exercises.explanation: Borrowed from English — common in informal goodbyes, especially over the phone.

lessons.title: How are you?
lessons.description: Ask after someone and answer back

exercises.prompt: How do you say "How are you?"
What does "很好" (hěn hǎo) mean?
Tap the phrase you hear
Build: "I'm very good, thank you."
exercises.answer: 我 很 好 謝謝
exercises.explanation: In Mandarin, adjectives don't take 是 — "I am good" is literally 我很好 (I very good).

exercises.prompt: Your friend asks 你好嗎? You're feeling fine. What do you say?
"不錯" (bú cuò) literally "not wrong" — it means ___
exercises.explanation: Common, slightly understated way to answer "how are you?" — like English "not bad."

exercises.prompt: the response with its tone
Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: Listen for 我 (wǒ, third tone — dipping) vs 你 (nǐ) and 他 (tā).

exercises.prompt: What does "你呢" (nǐ ne) mean?
exercises.explanation: 呢 (ne) bounces a question back. After answering 我很好, add 你呢 to ask the same of the other person.

exercises.prompt: Build: "How are you? And you?" — answer the first question with "and you?"
exercises.answer: 我 很 好 你 呢

exercises.prompt: "馬馬虎虎" (mǎ mǎ hū hū) literally "horse horse tiger tiger" means ___
exercises.explanation: A fun idiom — when neither good nor bad, you're "horse-tiger."

lessons.title: Polite phrases
lessons.description: Thank you, sorry, and you're welcome

exercises.prompt: How do you say "thank you"?
What does "對不起" mean?
"不客氣" (bú kè qi) means ___
exercises.explanation: Literally "don't be polite" — the standard reply to 謝謝.

exercises.prompt: each polite phrase
Someone says 對不起 to you. What's the natural reply?
exercises.explanation: 沒關係 (méi guān xi) means "it doesn't matter / it's okay" — the standard answer to an apology.

exercises.prompt: Tap the phrase you hear
"請" (qǐng) means ___
exercises.explanation: Place 請 at the start of a request to be polite, e.g. 請坐 (please sit).

exercises.prompt: What does "請坐" (qǐng zuò) mean?
Build: "Sorry, thank you."
Which is more emphatic for "thank you very much"?
exercises.explanation: 非常 (fēi cháng) = extremely; 感謝 (gǎn xiè) is a more formal "thanks." Together: "thanks a lot."

exercises.prompt: "沒關係" (méi guān xi) means ___
Build: "Sorry, please wait a moment"
exercises.answer: 對不起 請 等 一下

lessons.title: Nice to meet you
lessons.description: Introduce yourself

exercises.prompt: What does "我叫" (wǒ jiào) mean?
Build: "I am called Xiao Ming"
"認識你很高興" means ___
exercises.explanation: Literally: "knowing you makes me happy."

exercises.prompt: What does "你叫什麼名字" mean?
exercises.explanation: Literally: "You called what name?" 名字 (míng zi) = name.

exercises.prompt: Build: "What is your name?"
exercises.answer: 你 叫 什麼 名字

exercises.prompt: the introduction phrase
Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 我叫 (wǒ jiào) — "I am called." Listen for the falling tone on 叫.

exercises.prompt: What's the difference between "我叫小明" and "我是小明"?
options: Both mean "my name is Xiao Ming" — 叫 is more common in casual intros
我叫 means "I want" and 我是 means "I am"
我叫 is past tense, 我是 is present tense
exercises.answer: Both mean "my name is Xiao Ming" — 叫 is more common in casual intros
exercises.explanation: 我叫 literally "I'm called" — natural, friendly. 我是 literally "I am" — slightly more formal.

exercises.prompt: "貴姓" (guì xìng) literally "honored surname" — used to ask ___
exercises.explanation: Polite way to ask someone's last name: 您貴姓? Reply with 我姓 + your surname.

exercises.prompt: Build: "Nice to meet you" (literally: meeting you very happy)
exercises.answer: 認識 你 很 高興

exercises.prompt: You meet someone new. They say 你好, 我叫王明. What do you say back?
options: 你好, 我叫... 認識你很高興
exercises.answer: 你好, 我叫... 認識你很高興
exercises.explanation: Mirror the greeting and add "nice to meet you" — that's the standard A1 introduction.

lessons.title: Dialogue: First day at school
lessons.description: Meet a new classmate and exchange greetings.

exercises.prompt: Meeting a classmate on your first day

turns.speaker: ming
turns.text: 你好！(nǐ hǎo)
turns.spokenText: 你好！

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Say hello back.
turns.answer: 你好！(nǐ hǎo)

turns.speaker: ming
turns.text: 你好嗎？(nǐ hǎo ma)
turns.spokenText: 你好嗎？

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Say you are very good.
turns.answer: 我很好。(wǒ hěn hǎo)

turns.speaker: ming
turns.text: 我叫小明。(wǒ jiào Xiǎo Míng)
turns.spokenText: 我叫小明。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Fill in: I'm called Lì.
turns.answer: 叫

turns.speaker: ming
turns.text: 認識你很高興。(rèn shi nǐ hěn gāo xìng)
turns.spokenText: 認識你很高興。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Say goodbye.
turns.answer: 再見！(zài jiàn)

topics.title: Numbers
topics.description: Count, ask how many, give your age

guide.intro: Mandarin numbers are wonderfully regular — once you know 1 to 10 and the word for "ten", you can build every number up to 99.

sections.text: One to ten
Building 11–99
After ten, numbers are built like math problems. Read characters left to right, multiplying anything before 十 and adding anything after.
Same trick goes further: 一百 (one hundred), 一千 (one thousand), 一萬 (ten thousand) — but Chinese groups large numbers in 萬 (10,000) rather than thousands.
Two: 二 vs 兩
Mandarin has two words for "two". 二 (èr) is the digit — used in counting, math, and phone numbers. 兩 (liǎng) means "a pair of" — used before measure words and quantities.

rows.translation: twenty (the number)
two people (with measure word)

sections.text: Asking how many
幾 (jǐ) asks "how many?" for small expected counts (under ~10). 多少 (duō shǎo) asks "how much/many?" for any quantity, including money and big numbers.

rows.translation: How old are you? (to a child)
How much money?

lessons.title: One to five
lessons.description: Count from 一 to 五

exercises.prompt: What is "三" (sān)?
How do you write "five"?
the digit
Which is "two"?
"四" (sì) means ___
exercises.explanation: 四 sounds similar to 死 (sǐ, "death") — for this reason 4 is sometimes considered unlucky in Chinese culture, like 13 in the West.

exercises.prompt: Tap the digit you hear
exercises.explanation: 三 (sān) — first tone, high and flat. Don't confuse with 四 (sì), fourth tone, sharp falling.

exercises.prompt: Tap the digit you hear
exercises.explanation: 四 (sì) is fourth tone — sharp falling. Compare to 三 (sān), high and flat.

exercises.prompt: Which two numbers sound similar but differ only in tone?
exercises.explanation: Both have the same final "-ān/-ì" feel — distinguish by tone: 三 high-flat, 四 sharp-falling.

exercises.prompt: Order the numbers from one to five
exercises.answer: 一 二 三 四 五

exercises.prompt: Which character means "one"?
exercises.explanation: Just one stroke — the simplest character in Chinese.

exercises.prompt: "五" (wǔ) means ___
Tap the digit you hear
exercises.explanation: 二 (èr) — fourth tone, sharp falling. Quick to say.

lessons.title: Six to ten
lessons.description: Count up to 十

exercises.prompt: What is "六" (liù)?
What is "九" (jiǔ)?
"十" (shí) means ___
digit to character
Which is "seven"?
Which is "eight"?
exercises.explanation: 八 (bā) sounds like 發 (fā, "to prosper") — making 8 the luckiest number in Chinese culture.

exercises.prompt: Tap the digit you hear
exercises.explanation: 九 (jiǔ) is third tone — dipping. Long and dramatic compared to other tones.

exercises.prompt: Tap the digit you hear
exercises.explanation: 十 (shí) is second tone — rising. Don't confuse with 四 (sì), fourth tone.

exercises.prompt: Order the numbers from six to ten
exercises.answer: 六 七 八 九 十

exercises.prompt: Which number is considered the luckiest in Chinese culture?
exercises.explanation: 八 (bā) rhymes with 發 (fā, "to prosper"). Phone numbers and license plates with many 8s sell at a premium.

exercises.prompt: "六" (liù) means ___
Order the digits in ascending order: 8, 6, 9, 7
exercises.answer: 六 七 八 九

lessons.title: Tens and beyond
lessons.description: Build bigger numbers

exercises.prompt: What is "二十" (èr shí)?
How do you write "fifteen"?
exercises.explanation: 十五 = 10 + 5. Order matters!

exercises.prompt: Build "thirty-three"
What is "七十二" (qī shí èr)?
exercises.explanation: Read left to right: 七 (7) × 十 (10) + 二 (2) = 72.

exercises.prompt: "九十九" (jiǔ shí jiǔ) is the number ___
How do you write "forty-five"?
exercises.explanation: 四十 = 40, then add 五 = 45. The pattern: tens-digit + 十 + units-digit.

exercises.prompt: the number
Build "sixty-eight"
What is "一百" (yì bǎi)?
exercises.explanation: 百 (bǎi) is the unit for hundreds — 一百 = 100, 二百 = 200.

exercises.prompt: Tap the number you hear
exercises.explanation: Listen for the order: 二十一 = 21 ("two-ten-one"), 十二 = 12 ("ten-two").

exercises.prompt: Build the number "twelve" — order matters!
exercises.explanation: 十二 = 10 + 2. Compare: 二十 = 2 × 10 = 20. The order of 十 and the digit reverses the meaning.

exercises.prompt: "五十" (wǔ shí) is the number ___

lessons.title: How old? How many?
lessons.description: Use numbers in real questions

exercises.prompt: What does "幾歲" (jǐ suì) mean?
"五歲" means ___ years old
What does "多少" (duō shǎo) mean?
Use 幾 or 多少? "How many people are in your family?"
options: 多少 — could be a big number
exercises.explanation: 幾 (jǐ) for under ~10, things you can count on fingers. 多少 (duō shǎo) for any quantity, including money and large numbers.

exercises.prompt: Build: "How old are you?" (to a child)
exercises.explanation: 幾歲 is for kids; for adults use 你多大?

exercises.prompt: "我二十歲" means "I am ___ years old"
exercises.explanation: No 是 needed — 我二十歲, not 我是二十歲. Age uses adjective-like structure.

exercises.prompt: Which question would you ask an adult their age?
exercises.explanation: 幾歲 is for children. 多大 (literally "how big") is the polite ask for adults.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 多少錢 (duō shǎo qián) — "how much money?" The phrase you'll use most when shopping.

exercises.prompt: the question word
Build: "I have three older brothers"
exercises.answer: 我 有 三 個 哥哥
exercises.explanation: Numbers always need a measure word before a noun: 三個哥哥, not 三哥哥.

lessons.title: Phone numbers & dates
lessons.description: Read digits one at a time

exercises.prompt: When reading a phone number aloud, how is each digit spoken?
options: One digit at a time, like "yī sān bā"
Grouped as full numbers, like "yī bǎi sān shí bā"
Skipped — only key ones are said
exercises.answer: One digit at a time, like "yī sān bā"
exercises.explanation: Phone numbers, addresses, and ID numbers are read digit-by-digit — same as in English.

exercises.prompt: When dictating a phone number, the digit "1" is often pronounced as ___ instead of "yī"
exercises.explanation: 么 (yāo) replaces 一 (yī) in spoken digit strings to avoid confusing 一 with 七 (qī). You'll hear it on the phone and at the bank.

exercises.prompt: "零" (líng) means ___
exercises.explanation: 零 is the formal zero. You'll also see 〇 (a circle) used in dates and ID numbers.

exercises.prompt: the digit
How do you say "the year 2024"?
exercises.explanation: Years are read digit-by-digit + 年 (nián, year). 二零二四年 = "two-zero-two-four year."

exercises.prompt: "月" (yuè) means ___
exercises.explanation: 月 by itself means moon/month. With a number: 一月 = January, 二月 = February.

exercises.prompt: Which is "March"?
exercises.explanation: Months are number + 月. 三月 = March (3rd month). Don't confuse 月 (month) with 日 (day).

exercises.prompt: Build the date: "May 6th" (5月 then day-number then 號)
exercises.answer: 五 月 六 號
exercises.explanation: 號 (hào) is the casual word for date/day. 日 (rì) is the formal equivalent — both follow the day number.

exercises.prompt: Tap the date you hear
exercises.explanation: Big to small: 六月 (June) comes before 十號 (10th). Don't reverse it like English "the 10th of June."

exercises.prompt: Chinese dates go in what order?
exercises.explanation: Chinese always reads dates from largest unit to smallest: 2024年5月6日. Same logic for time: hour first, minute last.

exercises.prompt: "今天幾月幾號?" asks ___
exercises.explanation: Literally: "Today which month, which date?" The everyday way to ask the date.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear

lessons.title: Dialogue: At the fruit market
lessons.description: Count fruit and ask how much things cost.

exercises.prompt: Buying apples at a market stand

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: 你好！(nǐ hǎo)
turns.spokenText: 你好！

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Ask how much (the apples cost).
turns.answer: 多少錢？(duō shao qián)

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: 五塊錢一個。(wǔ kuài qián yí ge)
turns.spokenText: 五塊錢一個。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Fill in the measure word: I want three (apples).
turns.answer: 個

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: 三個十五塊。(sān ge shí wǔ kuài)
turns.spokenText: 三個十五塊。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Hand over the money — say 'here you go'.
turns.answer: 給你。(gěi nǐ)

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: 謝謝，再見！(xiè xie, zài jiàn)
turns.spokenText: 謝謝，再見！

topics.title: Basics
topics.description: Yes, no, I, you, this, that

guide.intro: Mandarin has no verb conjugation, no plural endings, no genders, and no articles. Once you know the word order, the language gets out of your way.

sections.text: Word order: subject – verb – object
Just like English, a basic sentence puts the subject first, the verb second, and the object last.

rows.translation: I drink tea.
He eats rice.
I love you.

sections.text: Pronouns are simple
他 (he) and 她 (she) are pronounced exactly the same — only the writing changes. In speech, listeners use context.
The verb 是 (shì)
是 means "to be" — but only for nouns connecting to other nouns ("I am a student"). For adjectives, you don't use 是; you use 很 (hěn) instead, which means "very" but is often a placeholder.

rows.translation: I am a student.
I am good. (no 是!)

sections.text: Negation: 不 vs 沒
Use 不 (bù) for negating present and future actions, and for adjectives. Use 沒 (méi) for past actions and for the verb 有 ("to have").

rows.source: 我 不 喝 茶。
rows.translation: I don't drink tea.

rows.source: 我 沒 有 錢。
rows.translation: I don't have money.

sections.text: No tenses!
Mandarin verbs do not change form for past, present, or future. Time is shown by adding a time word (yesterday, tomorrow) or particles like 了 (le) for completion.

rows.source: 昨天 我 吃 米飯。
rows.translation: Yesterday I ate rice.

rows.source: 明天 我 吃 米飯。
rows.translation: Tomorrow I will eat rice.

lessons.title: Yes & no
lessons.description: Simple yes/no responses

exercises.prompt: How do you say "yes"?
Which character means "no" / "not"?
"不是" (bú shì) means ___
exercises.explanation: "不是" literally "is not" — a common way to say "no".

exercises.prompt: Mandarin has no single word for "yes/no." Instead, you reply with the ___
options: Verb itself, optionally negated with 不
exercises.answer: Verb itself, optionally negated with 不
exercises.explanation: Q: 你喝茶嗎? (Do you drink tea?) → A: 喝 (yes, drink) or 不喝 (no, don't drink). Mirror the verb.

exercises.prompt: the right negation: ___ 喝 茶。(I don't drink tea.)
exercises.explanation: 不 (bù) negates present/future and adjectives. 沒 (méi) is for past actions and 有.

exercises.prompt: the right negation: 我 ___ 有 錢。(I don't have money.)
exercises.explanation: 有 (have) is the one verb that's always negated with 沒, never 不. 沒有 is fixed.

exercises.prompt: Build: "I am not a student"
exercises.answer: 我 不 是 學生

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 不 before a fourth tone (是, shì) shifts to second tone — pronounced "bú shì."

exercises.prompt: "對" (duì) literally "correct" — used like ___
exercises.explanation: 對 is the closest word to a casual "yes" — confirms what someone said. Reverse: 不對 ("no, that's wrong").

exercises.prompt: Build a negative reply to 你是中國人嗎? — "I am not Chinese"
exercises.answer: 我 不 是 中國 人
exercises.explanation: Mirror the verb 是 in the question and negate with 不: 不是. Don't add a separate "no" word.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 我沒有 = "I don't have." 沒 always pairs with 有, never 不.

lessons.title: I & you
lessons.description: Basic pronouns

exercises.prompt: What does "我" (wǒ) mean?
What does "你" (nǐ) mean?
"我們" (wǒ men) means ___
exercises.explanation: Add "們" to make a plural pronoun: 我們 = we.

exercises.prompt: What does "你們" (nǐ men) mean?
exercises.explanation: 你 + 們 = you (plural). English doesn't always distinguish singular/plural "you," but Mandarin does.

exercises.prompt: the pronoun
Build: "We are good"
exercises.explanation: Adjectives don't take 是 — 我們很好, not 我們是好.

exercises.prompt: What does "您" (nín) mean?
exercises.explanation: 您 is the formal "you" for elders, customers, strangers. The character has a 心 (heart) under 你 — "you with my heart."

exercises.prompt: The polite form of 你 is ___
exercises.explanation: 您 is used in shops, on the phone, with elders. Don't use it with close friends — feels stiff.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 我們 (wǒ men) — listen for the third tone on 我.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "I am Chinese"?
options: 我們 是 中國人
我 不 是 中國人

exercises.prompt: Build: "You all are my friends"
exercises.answer: 你們 是 我 的 朋友
exercises.explanation: 的 (de) makes a possessive: 我的 = "my," 你的 = "your."

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 您 (nín) — second tone, similar to 你 (nǐ, third tone). Listen for the rising vs dipping pitch.

lessons.title: He, she, they
lessons.description: Talk about other people

exercises.prompt: What does "他" (tā) mean?
What does "她" (tā) mean?
the pronoun
他 (he) and 她 (she) — what's the difference?
options: Different meanings (one is for adults, one for kids)
exercises.explanation: In speech, you can't tell — context decides. The 女 radical in 她 marks female; 它 (also tā) is for animals/things.

exercises.prompt: "他們" (tā men) means ___
exercises.explanation: 他們 is used for groups that are mixed-gender or all-male. 她們 is used only for all-female groups.

exercises.prompt: Which pronoun is used for animals or inanimate objects?
exercises.explanation: 它 (tā) — same pronunciation as 他/她 but written with the radical 宀 (roof). Use it for pets, things, weather.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 他們 (tā men) — first tone on 他, neutral on 們. In speech, identical to 她們.

exercises.prompt: Build: "She is my older sister"
exercises.answer: 她 是 我 姐姐

exercises.prompt: A group of three women — which is correct?
exercises.explanation: All-female groups use 她們. Add a single male and most speakers switch to 他們.

exercises.prompt: "她" is written with the radical ___ to mark female
exercises.explanation: 女 (nǚ) means "woman" — placed on the left side of 她 to distinguish it from 他.

exercises.prompt: Build: "They drink tea"
The pronoun for animals/things is ___
exercises.explanation: 它 (tā) — same sound as 他 and 她, but a different character. Use for pets, weather, things.

lessons.title: This & that
lessons.description: Point things out

exercises.prompt: What does "這" (zhè) mean?
What does "那" (nà) mean?
Build "This is my mom"
exercises.answer: 這 是 我 媽媽

exercises.prompt: What does "這個" (zhè ge) mean?
exercises.explanation: 個 (ge) is the all-purpose measure word. 這個 = "this (item)," 那個 = "that (item)."

exercises.prompt: the pointer

exercises.explanation: 這 (zhè) — fourth tone, sharp falling. 那 (nà) is also fourth tone but starts with "n."

exercises.prompt: You're at a market and want to ask the price of a specific item. Pointing at it, you say:
exercises.explanation: 這個 + 多少錢 = "this one, how much money?" The pointing-and-asking phrase you'll use most often shopping.

exercises.prompt: Build: "That is not my book"
exercises.answer: 那 不 是 我 的 書

exercises.prompt: Which means "these" (more than one)?
exercises.explanation: 些 (xiē) marks plural "these/those." 這些 = these, 那些 = those.

Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 這 (zhè) and 那 (nà) — both fourth tone. Distinguish by the 'zh' vs 'n' onset.

lessons.title: Mom & dad
lessons.description: Your closest people

exercises.prompt: How do you say "mom"?
How do you say "dad"?
"家" (jiā) means ___
the family word
Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 媽 (mā, first tone, high-flat) means "mom." Compare to 馬 (mǎ, third tone) — "horse"!

exercises.prompt: 媽 (mā) means "mom." What does 馬 (mǎ) mean?
exercises.explanation: Same syllable, different tone. 媽 (first tone) = mom; 馬 (third tone) = horse. Tones matter!

exercises.prompt: Build: "My mom and my dad"
exercises.answer: 我 媽媽 和 我 爸爸
exercises.explanation: 和 (hé) means "and" — used between nouns, not between full sentences.

exercises.prompt: "父母" (fù mǔ) means ___
exercises.explanation: 父 = father, 母 = mother. The compact, slightly formal way to say "parents."

exercises.prompt: What does "我愛我的家" mean?
exercises.explanation: 家 covers both "home" and "family" — context decides.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
Build: "My mom is at home"
exercises.answer: 我 媽媽 在 家
exercises.explanation: 在 (zài) marks location — "at." The structure is: subject + 在 + place.

lessons.description: Older and younger siblings

exercises.prompt: What does "哥哥" (gē ge) mean?
Which means "younger sister"?
the sibling
Why does Mandarin distinguish 哥哥 vs 弟弟 instead of using one word for "brother"?
options: Birth order matters in Chinese family relationships
It doesn't — they mean the same thing
exercises.answer: Birth order matters in Chinese family relationships
exercises.explanation: Chinese family terms encode age. You can't say "brother" without specifying older or younger — culture baked into vocabulary.

exercises.prompt: "姐姐" (jiě jie) means ___
Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 弟弟 (dì di) — fourth tone followed by neutral. Compare to 妹妹 (mèi mei), also fourth + neutral, but starts with "m."

exercises.prompt: Build: "I have one older sister"
exercises.answer: 我 有 一 個 姐姐
exercises.explanation: Numbers need a measure word: 一個姐姐, not 一姐姐.

exercises.prompt: Which means "younger brother"?
Build: "My older brother is at school"
exercises.answer: 我 哥哥 在 學校

exercises.prompt: "兄弟" (xiōng dì) means ___
exercises.explanation: 兄 = older brother, 弟 = younger brother. Together: brothers as a category — also used between male friends.

exercises.prompt: What does "爺爺" (yé ye) mean?
What does "奶奶" (nǎi nai) mean?
"老人" (lǎo rén) means ___
爺爺 and 奶奶 are which side of the family?
exercises.explanation: 爺爺 (paternal grandpa) and 奶奶 (paternal grandma). Mother's side has different terms — 外公 and 外婆.

exercises.prompt: the grandparent
"外婆" (wài pó) means ___
exercises.explanation: 外 (wài) literally "outside" — marks mother's-side relatives because traditionally a wife joined her husband's family.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 爺爺 (yé ye) — second tone followed by neutral. The 'y' sound starts both syllables.

exercises.prompt: What does "外公" (wài gōng) mean?
exercises.explanation: 外 (mom's side) + 公 (granddad).

exercises.prompt: Build: "My grandma is 80 years old"

exercises.explanation: Age skips 是: 我奶奶八十歲, not 我奶奶是八十歲.

exercises.prompt: Which is the most respectful way to address an elderly stranger?
exercises.explanation: 您 (nín) shows respect for elders. 你 with strangers older than you can feel rude.

exercises.prompt: "長輩" (zhǎng bèi) means ___
exercises.explanation: 長 (zhǎng) = senior, 輩 (bèi) = generation. Refers to older relatives collectively.

exercises.prompt: Build: "My maternal grandpa is at home"

exercises.prompt: Q: 你家有幾個人? (How many people are in your family?) Why 幾 and not 多少?

多少 only works with money
There is no rule — both are equally common
exercises.answer: Family is a small expected count — 幾 fits
exercises.explanation: 幾 for under ~10 (people, items). 多少 for big or unknown numbers (money, populations).

exercises.prompt: "全家" (quán jiā) means ___
exercises.explanation: 全 (quán) = entire/whole. Used when emphasizing "everyone in the family."

exercises.prompt: Someone shows you a photo of their family. They point and say 這是我媽媽. The natural response is:
exercises.explanation: 漂亮 (piào liang) means "beautiful." A common compliment when shown family photos.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: Listen for 四 (sì, fourth tone) — sharp falling — vs 十 (shí, second tone) rising.

lessons.description: Aunts, uncles, and the dog

exercises.prompt: What does "叔叔" (shū shu) mean?
exercises.explanation: Mandarin uncle terms split by age and side. 叔叔 specifically = dad's younger brother.

exercises.prompt: What does "阿姨" (ā yí) mean?
exercises.explanation: 阿姨 is also used as a friendly term for any middle-aged woman — like English "ma'am."

exercises.prompt: the relative
"表哥" (biǎo gē) means ___
exercises.explanation: 表 (biǎo) marks cousins from outside the direct family line — usually mom's-side cousins.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear

exercises.explanation: 貓 (māo) — first tone, sounds like "meow," easy to remember.

exercises.prompt: "寵物" (chǒng wù) means ___
exercises.explanation: 寵 = to spoil/dote, 物 = thing. Together: "a thing you spoil" — a pet.

exercises.prompt: Build: "I have one dog and one cat"

exercises.explanation: 只 (zhī) is the measure word for animals: 一隻狗, 一隻貓. (Not 個!)

exercises.prompt: What's the measure word for most animals (dogs, cats, birds)?
exercises.explanation: 只 (zhī) covers most small animals. Fish and snakes use 條 (long things). Don't use 個 for animals.

options: It's the measure word for cup-shaped servings
exercises.answer: It's the measure word for cup-shaped servings
exercises.explanation: Mandarin requires a measure word between number and noun. 杯 (cup) is used for any liquid in a cup.

exercises.prompt: Which means "steamed bun"?
exercises.explanation: 包 (bāo) means "to wrap" — a fluffy bun wrapping meat or vegetable filling.

exercises.prompt: the dish
"湯" (tāng) means ___
exercises.explanation: Soup is the borderline case for 喝/吃 — Mandarin uses 喝湯 ("drink soup").

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
What does "雞" (jī) mean?
exercises.explanation: 雞 (jī) sounds similar to 幾 (jǐ, "how many") — distinguish by tone.

exercises.prompt: the meat
"魚" (yú) means ___
exercises.explanation: 魚 (yú, second tone) sounds like 餘 (yú, "surplus") — fish are eaten at New Year for prosperity.

exercises.prompt: Build: "I want to eat dumplings and drink soup"
exercises.answer: 我 要 吃 餃子 和 喝 湯
exercises.explanation: Repeat the verb after 和 — Mandarin doesn't reuse one verb across two objects when they take different verbs.

topics.title: Common verbs
topics.description: Go, eat, want, like, see, listen

guide.intro: Mandarin verbs never change form. The same character is used for all persons and all times — context (and time words) does the heavy lifting.

sections.text: One verb, every form
Compare with English: "go / goes / went / will go" — Mandarin uses 去 for all of them. The action stays put; you add words around it.

rows.translation: I go / I am going.
He goes.
We go.
I went yesterday.

sections.text: Want vs. would-like: 要 / 想 / 喜歡
These three look interchangeable in English but have a clear pecking order in Mandarin.

rows: I want / I will (decisive, ordering food)
I would like / I am thinking about

rows.translation: I want coffee. (I'll have)

rows.source: 我 想 喝 咖啡。
rows.translation: I would like to drink coffee.
I like coffee.

sections.text: Completion: the 了 particle
Adding 了 (le) after a verb signals an action is finished. It's the closest thing Mandarin has to past tense — but it's really an aspect marker, not a tense.

rows.translation: I am eating.

rows.source: 我 吃 了 飯。
rows.translation: I ate. / I have eaten.

sections.text: Don't sprinkle 了 everywhere — for adjectives ("I am happy") or stative verbs, you don't use it. Save it for completed actions.

lessons.title: Go, come, eat
lessons.description: Three building-block verbs

exercises.prompt: Which means "to go"?
Which means "to come"?
"吃" (chī) means ___
the verb
去 (qù) and 來 (lái) — what's the key difference?
options: 去 means moving away from speaker; 來 means moving toward speaker
去 is past tense; 來 is future tense
去 is for people; 來 is for things
exercises.answer: 去 means moving away from speaker; 來 means moving toward speaker
exercises.explanation: Same as English go/come — perspective from the speaker.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 去 (qù) — fourth tone, sharp falling. Compare to 來 (lái), second tone rising.

exercises.prompt: Build: "I go to school"
Build: "He comes to my home"
exercises.answer: 他 來 我 家

exercises.prompt: Mandarin verbs change form for ___
exercises.explanation: 我去, 你去, 他去, 我們去 — same verb every time. Time and number come from other words.

exercises.prompt: "喝" (hē) means ___
Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 去吃飯 = "go eat" — verb chains in Mandarin string actions in sequence.

lessons.title: Want & like
lessons.description: Express what you wish for

exercises.prompt: What does "喜歡" (xǐ huan) mean?
What does "要" (yào) mean?
Build "I like tea"
Pick the right verb: ordering at a café — "I'll have a coffee."
options: 我要 一 杯 咖啡
我想 一 杯 咖啡
我喜歡 一 杯 咖啡
我有 一 杯 咖啡
exercises.answer: 我要 一 杯 咖啡
exercises.explanation: 要 (yào) is decisive — "I want / I'll have." Use it when ordering. 想 (xiǎng) is softer ("would like").

exercises.prompt: Pick the right verb: "I'd like to drink tea." (softer wish)
exercises.explanation: 想 + verb = "would like to (verb)." Notice: 想 needs another verb after it. 要 can stand alone with a noun.

exercises.prompt: the desire-verb
Tap what you hear
"愛" (ài) means ___
exercises.explanation: 愛 is stronger than 喜歡. Reserved for family, partners, deep affection — though usage is loosening among young Chinese.

exercises.prompt: Build: "I would like to go to school"
exercises.answer: 我 想 去 學校

exercises.prompt: What's wrong with: "我喜歡一杯咖啡"?
options: 喜歡 means general preference, not a one-time order
杯 is not a measure word
exercises.answer: 喜歡 means general preference, not a one-time order
exercises.explanation: 喜歡 = "I like coffee in general." To order one cup, use 要: 我要一杯咖啡.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 想 (xiǎng, third tone) — listen for the dipping pitch. Don't confuse with 要 (yào, fourth tone falling).

exercises.prompt: When ordering at a restaurant, the most natural verb is ___
exercises.explanation: 要 (yào) signals decisive intent — perfect for ordering. 想 sounds more like "considering it."

lessons.title: See & listen
lessons.description: Senses and observation

exercises.prompt: What does "看" (kàn) mean?
Which means "to listen"?
"說" (shuō) means ___
the sense-verb
What does "看書" (kàn shū) mean?
exercises.explanation: 看 covers seeing, looking, watching, AND reading — context decides. 看書 = read a book; 看電影 = watch a movie.

exercises.prompt: What does "聽音樂" (tīng yīn yuè) mean?
Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 聽 (tīng) — first tone, high and flat. Don't confuse with 停 (tíng, "stop").

exercises.prompt: Build: "I am reading a book"
exercises.answer: 我 在 看 書
exercises.explanation: 在 + verb = ongoing action ("am doing"). It marks the present continuous.

exercises.prompt: "看電影" (kàn diàn yǐng) means ___
exercises.explanation: 電 = electric, 影 = shadow. Together: "electric shadows" — a movie.

exercises.prompt: Which verb pair are you most likely to confuse?

topics.title: Time
topics.description: Days, hours, and when things happen

guide.intro: Time words go at the start of a sentence or right after the subject — never at the end like English. "Tomorrow I go" is the natural Mandarin order.

sections.text: Days are math
Days of the week are 星期 (xīngqī, "week") + the digit. So 星期一 is week-1 (Monday), 星期二 is week-2 (Tuesday), and so on through 星期六. Sunday is the odd one out: 星期天 or 星期日.
Telling time
Hours use 點 (diǎn, "o'clock"), minutes use 分 (fēn). Half-past is 半 (bàn). "Quarter" is 一刻 (yí kè) for :15 and 三刻 for :45.

rows.translation: 3 o'clock

sections.text: Time-words come first
In Mandarin, time goes before the verb. Compare:

rows.source: 我 明天 去 學校。
rows.translation: I am going to school tomorrow.

rows.source: 他 今天 不 來。
rows.translation: He is not coming today.

sections.text: A handy memory trick: Chinese says time in big-to-small order — year, month, day, hour, minute. The opposite of how dates are spoken in English.

exercises.prompt: Build: "I will go to school tomorrow"

By adding 是 before the verb

exercises.explanation: Mandarin verbs are fixed. Time words do all the heavy lifting — add 昨天 for past, 明天 for future.

topics.title: Questions
topics.description: Who, what, when, why, how

guide.intro: Mandarin questions are unusually friendly to learners — there's no auxiliary "do/does", no inversion. The word order stays the same as a statement.

sections.text: The 嗎 particle
For yes/no questions, take a statement and add 嗎 (ma) at the end. That's it. No reordering, no auxiliary verb.

rows.translation: You drink tea.

rows.source: 你 喝 茶 嗎？
rows.translation: Do you drink tea?

sections.text: Question words stay put
For information questions (who, what, where), put the question word exactly where the answer would go. No fronting like English.

rows.translation: Who are you? (You are who?)
What are you drinking?
Where are you?
Why is he coming?

sections.text: Common question words
A-not-A questions
A second way to ask yes/no questions: repeat the verb with 不 between. It's a touch more direct than 嗎.

rows.source: 你 是不是 學生？
rows.translation: Are you a student or not?
Do you drink tea or not?

sections.text: Don't mix patterns: 你是不是學生嗎？ is wrong. Pick one of the two question forms.

exercises.answer: You can't combine A-not-A with 嗎 — pick one
exercises.explanation: A-not-A and 嗎 are two ways to form yes/no questions. Don't mix them.

exercises.explanation: Add 嗎 at the end. Yes/no questions don't change word order.

exercises.prompt: What does "北" (běi) mean?

the cardinal
What does "北京" (Běi jīng) literally mean?
exercises.explanation: 北 = north, 京 = capital. The name reflects the city's history. Compare 南京 (Nanjing) = "southern capital."

exercises.prompt: "南" (nán) means ___
Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 東 (dōng) — first tone, high and flat. Different from 冬 (dōng, "winter") — same sound, different character.

exercises.explanation: Compounds combine the two: 東南 = east + south = southeast. Standard intercardinal pattern.

exercises.prompt: Build: "My home is in the north"
exercises.answer: 我 家 在 北 邊
exercises.explanation: 邊 (biān) means "side." 北邊 = the north side. Pair with 南邊, 東邊, 西邊.

exercises.prompt: "西邊" (xī biān) means ___
In Chinese culture, which order are cardinal directions traditionally listed?
options: East, south, west, north (東南西北)
North, south, east, west (北南東西)
North, east, south, west (北東南西)
exercises.answer: East, south, west, north (東南西北)
exercises.explanation: 東南西北 — clockwise starting from east. The Chinese mnemonic order, different from English's "north-south-east-west."

exercises.prompt: "過馬路" (guò mǎ lù) means ___
exercises.explanation: 過 (guò) = pass through. 馬路 = main road. Useful when giving directions in cities.

exercises.prompt: "開車" (kāi chē) means ___
exercises.explanation: 開 = open/start. "Start the vehicle" — drive.

exercises.prompt: "天氣" (tiān qì) means ___

topics.title: Completed actions
topics.description: 了 for what just happened, 過 for what you've ever done

guide.intro: A1 introduced 了 briefly. A2 is where it really earns its keep. There are also two siblings to learn — 过 (experience) and 还没 (not yet) — that round out talking about the past.

sections.text: 了 — completed action
Tack 了 onto a verb to mark that the action is finished. It's the closest thing Mandarin has to a past tense, but technically it's an aspect marker — the action is complete, not necessarily long ago.

rows.translation: I am eating.

rows.source: 我 吃 了 飯。
rows.translation: I ate / I have eaten.
He came / he's here.

sections.text: Negation: 還沒 (not yet)
Don't pair 了 with 不/沒. To say "haven't done it", drop 了 and use 還沒 (hái méi):

rows.translation: I haven't eaten yet.
He hasn't come yet.

sections.text: 過 — experience marker
過 (guò) tags a verb as "have you ever done this in your life?" — it's about experience, not completion. Compare:

rows.source: 我 吃 過 北京 烤鴨。
rows.translation: I have eaten Peking duck (sometime).

rows.source: 我 吃 了 北京 烤鴨。
rows.translation: I ate Peking duck (just now).

sections.text: Rule of thumb: 了 = the action is wrapped up. 過 = at some point in your life this happened. They occasionally co-occur but you'll mostly pick one.

topics.title: Shopping
topics.description: Money, prices, and getting what you want

guide.intro: Real Chinese shopping is fast and friendly. Three phrases get you 80% of the way there: 多少钱 (how much), 太贵了 (too expensive), and 给我 (give me).

sections.text: Money words
Spoken Chinese uses 塊 (kuài) for the main currency unit; written and formal Chinese uses 元 (yuán). They're the same value — like "buck" vs "dollar". 毛 (máo) and 分 (fēn) are tenths and hundredths.

topics.title: Comparisons
topics.description: A is bigger than B — the 比 pattern

guide.intro: English uses "-er" or "more" for comparisons. Mandarin uses 比 (bǐ) — a single particle that does the same job, with a fixed word order: A 比 B + adjective.

sections.text: Basic pattern: A 比 B + adjective

rows.source: 我 比 他 高。
rows.translation: I am taller than him.

rows.source: 蘋果 比 香蕉 便宜。
rows.translation: Apples are cheaper than bananas.

rows.source: 今天 比 昨天 熱。
rows.translation: Today is hotter than yesterday.

sections.text: Don't add 很 / 不 / 是 to a 比 sentence. "我 比 他 很 高" is wrong — drop 很. The comparison itself does the work.
Even more: 更
Add 更 (gèng, "even more") before the adjective when comparing to an already-strong baseline:

rows.source: 他 比 我 更 高。
rows.translation: He is even taller than me.

sections.text: The most: 最
最 (zuì) before an adjective means "the most". No 比 needed — it's a superlative.

rows.translation: He is the tallest.

rows.source: 我 最 喜歡 茶。
rows.translation: I like tea the most.

sections.text: Negative: A 沒有 B + adjective
To say "A is NOT as ___ as B", flip to 沒有 (méi yǒu, "doesn't have"):

rows.source: 我 沒有 他 高。
rows.translation: I am not as tall as him.

topics.title: Connecting ideas
topics.description: And, but, because, so — stitch sentences together

guide.intro: Up to now most sentences have been one thought. A2 is where you start chaining: "I went and then I ate", "It rained but I went", "I'm tired because I worked". Mandarin makes this easy — a small set of connectors does most of the heavy lifting.

sections.text: 然後 — and then
然後 (rán hòu) chains two events in time. Use it to narrate sequences.

rows.source: 我 起床，然後 吃 早飯。
rows.translation: I get up, and then I eat breakfast.

sections.text: 但是 / 可是 — but
Both mean "but" with no real difference; 可是 is a touch more conversational.

rows.source: 我 想 去，但是 我 沒 時間。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù, dànshì wǒ méi shíjiān.
rows.translation: I want to go, but I don't have time.

sections.text: 因為...所以 — because...so
Mandarin often uses both halves where English uses just one ("I'm tired BECAUSE I worked" → 因為 我 工作 了，所以 我 很 累).

rows.source: 因為 下雨，所以 我 沒 去。
rows.pinyin: Yīnwèi xià yǔ, suǒyǐ wǒ méi qù.
rows.translation: Because it was raining, (so) I didn't go.

sections.text: You can drop one half if context is clear: "因為 下雨，我 沒 去" works too. The full pair just sounds slightly more emphatic.
或者 vs 還是 — both mean "or"
Easy mix-up. 或者 (huò zhě) goes in statements ("I want tea or coffee"). 還是 (hái shi) goes in questions ("Do you want tea or coffee?").

rows.source: 我 想 喝 茶 或者 咖啡。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng hē chá huòzhě kāfēi.
rows.translation: I want to drink tea or coffee. (statement)

rows.source: 你 想 喝 茶 還是 咖啡？
rows.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng hē chá háishi kāfēi?
rows.translation: Do you want tea or coffee? (choice question)

topics.title: The 把 construction
topics.description: Putting the object first to talk about what you do TO it

guide.intro: 把 (bǎ) is one of the most distinctive features of Mandarin grammar. It moves the object before the verb to say "take X and do something to it". You'll hear it constantly — and English doesn't have a clean equivalent.

sections.text: The basic shape

Normal Chinese order is Subject–Verb–Object. With 把, you reorder to Subject–把–Object–Verb–(extra). The "extra" part is crucial — 把 sentences almost never end on a bare verb. There has to be a result, location, or change attached.

rows: 我 把 门 关 上
他 把 苹果 吃 了
请 放 书 在 桌子 上
请 把 书 放 在 桌子 上

sections.text: When to use 把
Use 把 when you want to emphasize what HAPPENS TO a specific, known object — moving it, finishing it, changing it, putting it somewhere. Both speaker and listener know which object you mean.

rows.source: 我 把 作業 做 完 了。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ zuòyè zuò wán le.
rows.translation: I finished the homework.

rows.source: 請 把 窗戶 打 開。
rows.translation: Please open the window.

rows.source: 他 把 杯子 打 破 了。
rows.pinyin: Tā bǎ bēizi dǎ pò le.
rows.translation: He broke the cup.

sections.text: If you can't say what HAPPENS TO the object, don't use 把. "我 把 蘋果 喜歡" is wrong — 喜歡 (like) doesn't change the apple.
What can't follow 把
把 needs a verb that physically affects the object. Verbs that don't qualify: feeling/perception verbs (愛, 喜歡, 覺得, 知道), existence verbs (有, 是), and most stative or motion-only verbs (來, 去, 走).

rows.source: 我 喜歡 這 本 書。
rows.translation: I like this book. (NOT 我 把 这 本 书 喜欢)
He knows the answer. (NOT 他 把 答案 知道)

sections.text: Negation: 沒 / 不 goes BEFORE 把

rows.pinyin: Wǒ méi bǎ zuòyè zuò wán.
rows.translation: I didn't finish the homework.

rows.pinyin: Qǐng bú yào bǎ mén guān shàng.

topics.title: The 被 passive
topics.description: When something happens TO the subject — usually unpleasantly

guide.intro: 被 (bèi) is the passive marker — "got / was done by". It's the mirror image of 把: where 把 puts the actor first and the patient mid-sentence, 被 puts the patient (victim) first.

sections.text: The basic shape
Pattern: Patient + 被 + (Agent) + Verb + result. The agent is optional — drop it if it's unknown or obvious.

rows.source: 我 的 手機 被 偷 了。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī bèi tōu le.
rows.translation: My phone was stolen. (no agent)

rows.source: 杯子 被 他 打 破 了。
rows.pinyin: Bēizi bèi tā dǎ pò le.
rows.translation: The cup was broken by him.

rows.source: 錢 被 老闆 拿走 了。
rows.pinyin: Qián bèi lǎobǎn ná zǒu le.
rows.translation: The money was taken by the boss.

sections.text: 把 vs 被 — same event, different POV

rows: 他 把 杯子 打 破 了
杯子 被 他 打 破 了
小偷 偷 了 我 的 手机
我 的 手机 被 (小偷) 偷 了

sections.text: Mandarin's 被 has a slightly negative or unfortunate flavor — it's used much more often for bad things (got stolen, broken, scolded) than for neutral or good ones. Sentences like "I was praised" (我 被 表揚 了) work but feel marked.
叫 / 讓 — informal alternatives
In speech, 叫 (jiào) or 讓 (ràng) often replace 被. They sound more casual — but unlike 被, they REQUIRE an agent.

rows.source: 我 的 錢 讓 他 拿走 了。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ de qián ràng tā ná zǒu le.
rows.translation: My money got taken by him.

rows.source: 他 叫 老師 批評 了。
rows.translation: He got scolded by the teacher.

sections.text: Negation
Same as 把 — put 沒 BEFORE 被.

rows.source: 我 的 手機 沒 被 偷。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī méi bèi tōu.
rows.translation: My phone wasn't stolen.

sections.text: Two flavors of 了
Mandarin uses 了 in two distinct slots, and 把 / 被 sentences often need both. Knowing which is which is the difference between a complete sentence and a fragment.

rows: Something is now different / new situation

rows.source: 他 吃 了 三 個 蘋果。
rows.pinyin: Tā chī le sān ge píngguǒ.
rows.translation: He ate three apples. (perfective 了₁ — action complete)
It's raining now. (sentence 了₂ — change of state, didn't use to be)

rows.source: 已經 下 了 三 天 雨 了。
rows.pinyin: Yǐjīng xià le sān tiān yǔ le.
rows.translation: It's been raining for three days. (BOTH 了 — completed duration AND ongoing relevance)

sections.text: Quick test: if the 了 hugs the verb (verb 了 object), it's 了₁. If the 了 is at the very end of the sentence, it's 了₂. Same character, different jobs.

topics.title: Giving with 給
topics.description: 給 as both "give" and a coverb meaning "for / to"

guide.intro: 给 (gěi) wears two hats. As a main verb it means "give". As a coverb sitting before another verb, it marks the recipient or beneficiary — "for someone", "to someone". Both uses are everywhere.

sections.text: 給 as main verb — "give"
Pattern: Subject + 給 + recipient + thing. Two objects in a row, recipient first.

rows.source: 我 給 他 一 本 書。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ gěi tā yì běn shū.
rows.translation: I gave him a book.

rows.source: 媽媽 給 我 錢。
rows.translation: Mom gave me money.

sections.text: 給 as coverb — "for / to"
Sandwiched before another verb, 給 marks who benefits or receives the action. Pattern: Subject + 給 + recipient + verb + object.

rows.source: 我 給 你 買 了 一 杯 咖啡。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ gěi nǐ mǎi le yì bēi kāfēi.
rows.translation: I bought you a coffee. (the buying is FOR you)

rows.source: 他 給 媽媽 打 電話。
rows.translation: He's calling mom. (the call is TO mom)

rows.source: 請 給 我 介紹 一下。
rows.translation: Please introduce (it) to me.

sections.text: Notice how 給 you 買 (buy for you) and 給 媽媽 打 電話 (call mom) both keep 給 + person BEFORE the main verb. English flips this around — Chinese is rigid about the order.
Common 給-verb pairings

rows: 给 X 打 电话

topics.title: How well? — 得 complement
topics.description: Modify a verb with how it was done — 得 + adjective

guide.intro: 得 (de) lets you describe the manner or degree of an action: not WHAT you did, but HOW WELL or HOW MUCH. It's the closest Mandarin gets to English adverbs.

sections.text: The basic pattern
Pattern: Subject + Verb + 得 + (very) + Adjective. Note the position of 很 — almost always required to keep the sentence sounding natural.

rows.source: 他 跑 得 很 快。
rows.translation: He runs very fast.

rows.source: 她 唱 得 很 好。
rows.translation: She sings very well.

rows.source: 我 睡 得 不 好。
rows.translation: I didn't sleep well.

sections.text: When the verb has an object
If your verb takes an object, you have to repeat the verb. Mandarin can't have an object AND a 得 phrase on the same verb. Pattern: Subject + Verb + Object, Verb + 得 + adjective.

rows.source: 他 說 中文 說 得 很 好。
rows.pinyin: Tā shuō Zhōngwén shuō de hěn hǎo.
rows.translation: He speaks Chinese very well. (literally: "speaks Chinese, speaks very well")

rows.source: 她 寫 字 寫 得 很 漂亮。
rows.pinyin: Tā xiě zì xiě de hěn piàoliang.
rows.translation: She writes characters beautifully.

sections.text: Common mistake: "他 說 中文 得 很 好" — wrong. The verb has to repeat. Or you can drop the object: "他 中文 說 得 很 好" also works.
Three different 得 / 的 / 地

rows: after a verb: how it was done
走 得 慢 — walks slowly

sections.text: All three are pronounced "de" (neutral tone) — only writing distinguishes them. Pay attention to position: 的 between nouns, 地 before verbs, 得 after verbs.
Negation: not 不 before 得 — 不 before the adjective

rows.source: 他 跑 得 不 快。
rows.translation: He doesn't run fast.

rows.source: 我 唱 得 不 好。
rows.translation: I don't sing well.

topics.title: Opinions & agreement
topics.description: I think, I believe, I agree — saying what you reckon

guide.intro: B1 means saying more than "I like" or "I want". You need ways to express opinions softly, agree, disagree, and ask people what THEY think. Three verbs do the heavy lifting: 觉得, 认为, and 看.

sections.text: 覺得 — feel / think (everyday)
覺得 (jué de) is the workhorse — "I feel / think that...". Use it for any soft, personal opinion. By far the most common in conversation.

rows.source: 我 覺得 這 個 電影 很 好。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ juéde zhè ge diànyǐng hěn hǎo.
rows.translation: I think this movie is good.

rows.source: 你 覺得 怎麼樣？
rows.translation: What do you think?

sections.text: 認為 — believe / hold (more formal)
認為 (rèn wéi) is firmer and more written — "I hold the view that...". Right for opinions on bigger issues, news, business, debate.

rows.source: 我 認為 這 個 計劃 不 行。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ rènwéi zhè ge jìhuà bù xíng.
rows.translation: I don't think this plan will work.

rows.source: 專家 認為 經濟 會 好轉。
rows.translation: Experts believe the economy will improve.

sections.text: 看 — see / view (informal opinion ask)
看 (kàn) literally means "look", but "你 看 …" idiomatically means "in your view, …". Used to gently ask someone's take.

rows.source: 你 看 我 該 怎麼 辦？
rows.pinyin: Nǐ kàn wǒ gāi zěnme bàn?
rows.translation: What do you think I should do?

rows.source: 我 看 應該 沒 問題。
rows.translation: I think it should be fine.

sections.text: Agreeing & disagreeing
Chinese conversation tends to soften disagreement. "我 不 太 同意" (I don't really agree) is gentler and more common than a flat "不 同意".

lessons.title: I think (覺得)
lessons.description: Soft personal opinions

exercises.prompt: What does "我 覺得" (wǒ juéde) mean?
Build "I think this movie is very good"
exercises.answer: 我 覺得 這 個 電影 很 好

exercises.prompt: How do you ask "What do you think?"
options: 你 覺得 怎麼樣
exercises.answer: 你 覺得 怎麼樣

exercises.prompt: Build "I think his Chinese is pretty good"
exercises.answer: 我 覺得 他 的 中文 還 不錯
exercises.explanation: 還 不錯 — "pretty good / not bad". A B1 staple, milder than 很 好.

exercises.prompt: "我 覺得 這 個 價格 太 貴 了"
options: I think this price is too expensive
I'm willing to pay this price
This price is fine for me
exercises.answer: I think this price is too expensive

exercises.prompt: the soft-opinion phrase

pairs.left: 我 覺得 還 行
我 覺得 不 太 好
pairs.right: I don't really think it's good

pairs.left: 我 覺得 挺 好 的
我 覺得 沒 問題

exercises.prompt: Fill: "你 ___ 這 個 計劃 怎麼樣？" ("What do you think of this plan?")
Build "I felt the movie was a little long"
exercises.answer: 我 覺得 那 個 電影 有點 長
exercises.explanation: 有點 + adjective — "a little (negative tinge)". 有點 長 = a bit too long.

exercises.prompt: How do you politely disagree with someone's opinion using 覺得?
options: 我 覺得 不 是 這 樣
Both work but the second is more natural
exercises.answer: Both work but the second is more natural
exercises.explanation: 我 不 覺得 ... is grammatical but blunt. 我 覺得 不 是 這 樣 ("I don't think that's the case") softens the disagreement.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear

lessons.title: I believe (認為)
lessons.description: Firmer, more formal opinions

exercises.prompt: How does "認為" differ from "覺得"?
options: 認為 is firmer / more formal; 覺得 is everyday
認為 only goes in questions
exercises.answer: 認為 is firmer / more formal; 覺得 is everyday

exercises.prompt: Build "I don't think this plan will work"
exercises.answer: 我 認為 這 個 計劃 不 行

exercises.prompt: "專家 認為" means "___ believe"
Build "I believe this is a chance worth trying"
exercises.answer: 我 認為 這 是 一 個 值得 試 一 試 的 機會
exercises.explanation: 值得 + V + 一 + V — "worth Ving once / worth a V". B1 idiom for evaluating chances.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right register: a news article on the economy
options: 經濟 學家 覺得 經濟 會 好轉
經濟 學家 認為 經濟 會 好轉
經濟 學家 看 經濟 會 好轉
經濟 學家 想 經濟 會 好轉
exercises.answer: 經濟 學家 認為 經濟 會 好轉
exercises.explanation: 認為 is the formal/written verb. 覺得 sounds too colloquial for news.

exercises.prompt: the 覺得 / 認為 to the right context

pairs.left: 我 覺得 這 個 菜 好 吃
專家 認為 這 個 政策 不 行
我 覺得 你 應該 休息
學者 認為 這 是 歷史 事件

exercises.prompt: Fill: "老闆 ___ 這 個 專案 應該 取消" (firmer opinion verb)
"我 不 認為 他 是 對 的"
exercises.explanation: 我 不 認為 — direct, formal. Stronger than 我 覺得 不 ...

exercises.prompt: Build "Many people believe traveling is a kind of education"
exercises.answer: 很 多 人 認為 旅行 是 一 種 教育

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
Which best matches "In my view, the climate is changing"?
options: 我 覺得 氣候 在 變化
我 認為 氣候 在 變化
我 看 氣候 在 變化
Any of these work in different registers
exercises.answer: Any of these work in different registers
exercises.explanation: All three opinion verbs work; 認為 is firmest, 覺得 most casual, 看 most idiomatic.

lessons.title: Agree & disagree
lessons.description: 同意, 不同意, and softer versions

exercises.prompt: the phrase
Which softens disagreement?
options: 我 不 太 同意
我 完全 不 同意
我 覺得 不 對
exercises.answer: 我 不 太 同意
exercises.explanation: 不 太 (not very) is the standard softener — politer than a flat "不".

exercises.prompt: Build "You're right, this makes sense"
exercises.answer: 你 說 得 對 ， 這 很 有 道理

exercises.prompt: "我 完全 同意 你"
Build "Sorry, I really can't agree"
exercises.answer: 對不起 我 實在 不 能 同意
exercises.explanation: 實在 (shí zài) — "really, honestly". Politely strengthens disagreement.

exercises.prompt: Fill: "這 個 想法 ___ 道理" ("makes sense" — verb that means 'has')
the response to its strength

pairs.left: 我 也 這麼 想
我 不 太 同意
我 完全 不 同意

exercises.prompt: Pick the politest disagreement:
options: 你 說 得 不 對
我 覺得 不 一定 是 這 樣
不 是 這 樣
exercises.answer: 我 覺得 不 一定 是 這 樣
exercises.explanation: 我 覺得 不 一定 ... — "I think it's not necessarily ...". Hedge, hedge, hedge.

exercises.prompt: Build "Both views make sense"
exercises.answer: 兩 種 看法 都 有 道理

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
What does "我 同意 你 的 看法 ， 不過 ..." signal?
options: Polite agreement followed by a counterpoint
exercises.answer: Polite agreement followed by a counterpoint
exercises.explanation: 不過 = "however / but". Standard "yes, but ..." Chinese debate move.

lessons.title: Asking for opinions
lessons.description: 你看 / 你怎麼想

exercises.prompt: What does "你 看 我 該 怎麼 辦？" mean?
options: What do you think I should do?
exercises.answer: What do you think I should do?

exercises.prompt: Build "I think it should be fine"
exercises.answer: 我 看 應該 沒 問題

exercises.prompt: Tap the question you hear
Build "What's your view on this issue?"
exercises.answer: 你 對 這 個 問題 怎麼 看
exercises.explanation: 對 X 怎麼 看 — "how do you see / view X". The pattern that turns 看 into the opinion verb.

exercises.prompt: "我 看 不 行"
exercises.explanation: 我 看 + assertion = "as I see it". Idiomatic; nothing to do with literal vision.

exercises.prompt: the way to ask for an opinion

pairs.left: 你 覺得 怎麼樣

pairs.right: How do you feel about it?

pairs.left: 你 的 看法 是 什麼

exercises.prompt: Fill: "你 ___ 這 件 事 怎麼 看" ("toward / about")
Pick the most natural way to ask a friend's casual take:
options: 您 對 此 有 何 看法
請問 您 的 高 見
exercises.explanation: 你 看 呢 — short, casual, friend-to-friend. The other options are formal/written/honorific.

exercises.prompt: Build "In your view, which restaurant is better?"
exercises.answer: 你 看 哪 家 餐廳 比較 好

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
"我 覺得 應該 沒 什麼 問題"

I don't think there's a problem
All of the above are reasonable in context
exercises.answer: All of the above are reasonable in context
exercises.explanation: "應該 沒 什麼 問題" is hedging — "probably no issue". Translation depends on context.

topics.title: Telling a story
topics.description: Sequencing past events with 著 and directional verbs

guide.intro: When you narrate a story you need ways to set the scene ("she was sitting"), describe motion ("he walked in"), and string events together. 着 handles ongoing states; directional complements like 上来 and 下去 handle motion in space.

sections.text: 著 — ongoing state
著 (zhe) attached to a verb means "in the state of doing". It's NOT the same as English -ing — 著 emphasizes a held position or background condition, often setting the scene.

rows.translation: He is standing. (in a standing state)
The door is open. (held open)

rows.source: 她 笑 著 說。
rows.translation: She said with a smile. (smiling-while-speaking)

sections.text: 著 vs 在: 在 means "actively doing right now" ("我 在 吃飯" — I'm eating). 著 means "in this state" ("門 開 著" — the door's open). For narration, 著 sets the scene; 在 reports a live action.
Directional complements: 上 / 下 / 進 / 出 / 來 / 去
Six little words combine into rich verbs of motion. Pair a base direction (up/down/in/out) with 來 (toward speaker) or 去 (away from speaker).

rows.source: 他 走 進來 了。
rows.translation: He walked in.

rows.source: 她 跑 出去 了。
rows.translation: She ran out.
Please come up.

sections.text: Figurative directionals — 起來 / 下去 / 出來
Directional complements stretch beyond physical motion. Attached to non-motion verbs, they signal phase or aspect: starting, continuing, or coming-to-clarity.

rows: 看 起来 很 累 — looks tired

rows.source: 我 終於 想 出來 了。
rows.translation: I finally figured it out.

rows.source: 請 你 說 下 去。
rows.translation: Please keep talking.

rows.source: 他 突然 笑 起來 了。
rows.translation: He suddenly started to laugh.

sections.text: Sequencing words
A2's 然後 still works, but B1 stories add 先...再... (first...then...), 最後 (finally), 突然 (suddenly), and 後來 (afterward — for events further apart).

rows.source: 我 先 吃飯，再 看 電影。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ xiān chīfàn, zài kàn diànyǐng.
rows.translation: First I'll eat, then watch a movie.
It suddenly started to rain.

rows.source: 後來 他 搬 走 了。
rows.translation: Afterward, he moved away.

exercises.prompt: Distinguish: 我 吃 了 餃子 vs 我 吃 過 餃子

First is future, second is past
First is question, second is statement
exercises.answer: First: I ate dumplings (specific occasion). Second: I have eaten dumplings (ever, in my life)
exercises.explanation: 了 = perfective (one occasion completed). 過 = experiential (have you ever).

turns.speaker: yu

我你買茶具一套了 (Wǒ nǐ mǎi chájù yī tào le)

levels.name: B2 — Upper Intermediate
levels.description: Discuss abstract topics, defend opinions, and handle the news, the workplace, and contemporary Chinese culture.

topics.title: Expressing opinions
topics.description: Hedge, agree, push back, and stack reasons

guide.intro: At B2 you stop just stating opinions and start structuring them — adding nuance, layering reasons, and naming the side you fall on. Three patterns will carry most of your opinion-talk for the rest of your Chinese life: 不仅…而且 (not only…but also), 我觉得…比较 (I think…relatively), and 一方面…另一方面 (on one hand…on the other).

sections.text: 不僅…而且 — not only…but also

不僅 (bù jǐn) sets up the first half of a two-part claim, and 而且 (ér qiě) adds the second, usually stronger, point. The two halves can share a subject (which sits in front) or have different subjects (which sit after each particle).

rows.source: 他不僅會說中文，而且會說日語。
rows.pinyin: Tā bù jǐn huì shuō Zhōngwén, ér qiě huì shuō Rìyǔ.
rows.translation: He not only speaks Chinese, but also Japanese.

rows.source: 這家餐廳不僅便宜，而且很好吃。
rows.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng bù jǐn piányi, ér qiě hěn hǎo chī.
rows.translation: This restaurant is not only cheap but also delicious.

rows.source: 不僅我喜歡他，而且我妹妹也喜歡他。
rows.pinyin: Bù jǐn wǒ xǐhuan tā, ér qiě wǒ mèimei yě xǐhuan tā.
rows.translation: Not only do I like him, but my sister does too.

sections.text: Common mistake: dropping 而且 and joining with a comma. In Mandarin, 不僅 always pairs with 而且 (or 也 / 還). "他不僅高，帥" sounds incomplete.
Softening: 我覺得 + 比較

比較 (bǐ jiào) means "relatively" or "fairly" — it takes the edge off an opinion the way "kind of" does in English. Pair it with 我覺得 (wǒ jué de, "I feel") for a polite, hedged tone that won't sound confrontational.

rows.source: 我覺得這個想法比較有意思。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ jué de zhè ge xiǎngfǎ bǐ jiào yǒu yì si.
rows.translation: I think this idea is fairly interesting.

rows.source: 我覺得他說的比較有道理。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ jué de tā shuō de bǐ jiào yǒu dào lǐ.
rows.translation: I think what he said makes a fair amount of sense.

sections.text: Two sides: 一方面…另一方面
Use 一方面 (yī fāng miàn)…另一方面 (lìng yī fāng miàn) to lay out two sides of the same issue — the closest Mandarin gets to "on one hand…on the other hand".

rows.source: 一方面工作很累，另一方面工資也不高。
rows.pinyin: Yī fāng miàn gōng zuò hěn lèi, lìng yī fāng miàn gōng zī yě bù gāo.
rows.translation: On one hand the work is tiring, on the other hand the pay isn't great either.

items: 我同意你的看法 — I agree with your view
我不太同意 — I don't quite agree
我有不同的看法 — I have a different view

lessons.title: I think, I feel
lessons.description: Stating a view with 覺得 and 認為

exercises.prompt: What's the difference between 覺得 and 認為?
options: 覺得 is more casual/feeling-based; 認為 is more considered/formal
覺得 means "think"; 認為 means "feel"
exercises.answer: 覺得 is more casual/feeling-based; 認為 is more considered/formal

exercises.prompt: Build "I think this movie is really worth watching"
exercises.answer: 我 覺得 這部 電影 很 值得 看

exercises.prompt: "我認為他說得有道理" means ___
exercises.answer: I think what he said makes sense
acceptableAnswers: I believe what he said makes sense
I think he has a point

exercises.prompt: Which is the most natural way to soften "I think it's expensive"?
exercises.explanation: 有點兒 (yǒu diǎnr) before an adjective is what does the softening — without it, 我覺得貴 is grammatical but blunt.

exercises.prompt: Build a more formal opinion: "I personally believe this idea is worth considering"
exercises.answer: 我 個人 認為 這個 想法 值得 考慮
exercises.explanation: 我個人認為 (wǒ gè rén rèn wéi) lifts the register — 個人 ("personally") plus 認為 sounds essay-like; 我覺得 would be the casual swap.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks 你覺得這家餐廳怎麼樣? Which reply HEDGES the most?
exercises.explanation: 還行吧 ("it's okay, I guess") plus 比較一般 ("relatively average") is the classic Chinese hedge — neither praising nor trashing.

exercises.prompt: "在我看來，這件事沒那麼簡單" means ___
exercises.answer: In my view, this matter isn't that simple
acceptableAnswers: From my perspective, it's not that simple
The way I see it, this isn't so simple
In my opinion, this isn't that simple
exercises.explanation: 在我看來 (zài wǒ kàn lái) — "in my view". A common B2 opener for stating an opinion with a touch more weight than 我覺得.

exercises.prompt: the opinion-opener to its register

pairs.right: Stating a view: in my view
Older / literary: as I see it

exercises.prompt: Build "I think this question deserves more thought"
exercises.answer: 我 覺得 這個 問題 值得 多 想 一下

exercises.prompt: Pick the BLUNT version (avoid in polite settings):
options: 我覺得他說得有點兒不對
exercises.explanation: Bare 不對 with no hedge is direct to the point of rude. The other three all soften with 覺得, 不太, or 可能.

exercises.prompt: Convert casual "我覺得對" into a more formal/considered opinion. The blank should fill in: "我 ___ 這個觀點是正確的"
exercises.explanation: Swap 覺得 → 認為 to lift register. 我認為這個觀點是正確的 — "I believe this view is correct".

exercises.prompt: Tap the opener you hear
exercises.spokenText: 在 我 看 來
options: 在 我 看 來
在 我 來 看
看 來 我 在
我 看 在 來
exercises.answer: 在 我 看 來
exercises.explanation: 在我看來 (zài wǒ kàn lái) is a fixed four-syllable opener — the order is locked.

lessons.title: Not only, but also
lessons.description: Stack reasons with 不僅…而且

exercises.prompt: Build "This restaurant is not only cheap but also delicious"
exercises.answer: 這家 餐廳 不僅 便宜 而且 很 好吃

exercises.prompt: Pick the best translation for "Not only do I like him, my sister also likes him":
options: 不僅我喜歡他，而且我妹妹也喜歡他
exercises.answer: 不僅我喜歡他，而且我妹妹也喜歡他

exercises.prompt: "他不僅聰明，而且很努力" means ___
exercises.answer: He is not only smart but also hardworking
acceptableAnswers: Not only is he smart, he is also hardworking
He's not only clever but also diligent

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is GRAMMATICALLY WRONG?
exercises.explanation: 不僅 must pair with 而且 / 還 / 也. A bare comma is not enough — the second clause needs a connector.

exercises.prompt: 不僅 cannot pair with which of these?
exercises.explanation: 但是 introduces contrast ("but"). 不僅 needs an additive partner: 而且, 還, or 也.

exercises.prompt: Convert single-clause to compound: "He's hardworking and talented" → use 不僅...而且
exercises.answer: 他 不僅 努力 而且 有 才華

exercises.prompt: "這部電影不僅好看，___ 很有意義"
exercises.explanation: Any of 而且 / 還 / 也 completes the 不僅 pattern. The most common written choice is 而且.

exercises.prompt: Build "This phone is not only expensive but also doesn't have a good battery"
exercises.answer: 這 部 手機 不僅 貴 而且 電池 也 不 好

exercises.prompt: Best translation for "Not only does she sing, she also dances":
options: 她不僅會唱歌，還會跳舞
exercises.answer: 她不僅會唱歌，還會跳舞

exercises.prompt: "內卷不僅影響年輕人，還影響整個社會" means ___
exercises.answer: Involution doesn't only affect young people, it also affects the whole society
acceptableAnswers: Involution affects not only young people but the whole society
Not only does involution affect young people, it affects all of society
exercises.explanation: 內卷 — the cutthroat competition meme. The 不僅...還 frame stacks two scopes of impact.

exercises.prompt: Tap the connector you hear
exercises.explanation: 不僅 (bù jǐn) and 不但 (bù dàn) are near-synonyms — 不但 is slightly more spoken. 不過 means "however" and 不然 means "otherwise". Listen for the second syllable.

lessons.title: Agree & disagree
lessons.description: 同意, 反對, and the polite middle

exercises.prompt: the phrase to its meaning
Which is the most polite way to disagree?
exercises.explanation: Literally "I have a different view" — softer than a direct "you're wrong".

exercises.prompt: Build "I basically agree with your point of view"
exercises.answer: 我 基本 同意 你 的 看法

exercises.prompt: the agreement to its strength

pairs.right: Soft: I feel that way too

exercises.prompt: the disagreement to its tone

pairs.right: Pushback: I wouldn't put it that way

exercises.prompt: Build a hedged disagreement: "I'm not entirely sure I agree with this view"
exercises.answer: 我 不 太 確定 我 同意 這 個 看法

exercises.prompt: Your boss states a view in a meeting. Which response is appropriate?
options: 您的看法很有道理，不過我有一點不同意見
exercises.answer: 您的看法很有道理，不過我有一點不同意見
exercises.explanation: Concede first (有道理), then introduce disagreement with 不過 ("however") and a softener like 一點 — the standard formula for pushback in formal settings.

exercises.prompt: "話是這麼說，可是…" means ___
exercises.explanation: 話是這麼說，可是… is the most common spoken way to concede a point and pivot to your real objection.

exercises.prompt: Pick the strongest agreement:
Build a hedge: "To some extent, I agree with you"
exercises.answer: 在 某 種 程度 上 我 同意 你
exercises.explanation: 在某種程度上 — "to a certain degree" — the classic essay hedge before partial agreement.

exercises.prompt: Tap the phrase you hear
exercises.spokenText: 我 不 太 同意
options: 我 不 太 同意
exercises.answer: 我 不 太 同意
exercises.explanation: 不太 + verb is the soft-disagreement frame. Hear it as a polite "not quite" rather than "not at all".

lessons.title: Two sides of an issue
lessons.description: 一方面…另一方面 and 既…又

exercises.prompt: What does "一方面…另一方面" mean?
options: On one hand… on the other hand
exercises.answer: On one hand… on the other hand

exercises.prompt: Build "On one hand the work is tiring, on the other hand the pay isn't high"
exercises.answer: 一方面 工作 很 累 另一方面 工資 也 不 高

exercises.prompt: "她既聰明又漂亮" means ___
exercises.answer: She is both smart and beautiful
acceptableAnswers: She is smart as well as beautiful
exercises.explanation: 既…又 (jì…yòu) stacks two qualities of the same subject — "both…and".

exercises.prompt: Which best translates "It's expensive but worth it"?
Build "On one hand the salary is high, on the other hand the pressure is also great"
exercises.answer: 一方面 工資 很 高 另一方面 壓力 也 很 大

exercises.prompt: "這個工作既穩定又有意思" means ___
exercises.answer: This job is both stable and interesting
acceptableAnswers: This job is stable and also interesting
It's a job that is both steady and interesting
exercises.explanation: 既...又 — stacks two qualities of one subject. 既 X 又 Y means "both X and Y".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is GRAMMATICALLY WRONG?
exercises.explanation: 既 pairs with 又 (not 也). 既 X 又 Y is the locked frame.

exercises.prompt: Build "Studying abroad has both advantages and disadvantages"
exercises.answer: 出國 留學 既 有 好處 又 有 壞處

exercises.prompt: the two-sided pattern

pairs.right: On one hand…on the other (separate clauses)

exercises.prompt: "凡事都有兩面" (fán shì dōu yǒu liǎng miàn) means ___
acceptableAnswers: There are two sides to everything
exercises.explanation: A common B2 set phrase to open a balanced opinion. 凡事 = every matter.

exercises.prompt: Build "Although AI is convenient, it also brings problems"
exercises.answer: 雖然 人工智慧 很 方便 但是 也 帶 來 一些 問題

exercises.prompt: Pick the most balanced essay-style opening:
options: 凡事都有兩面：一方面…另一方面…
exercises.answer: 凡事都有兩面：一方面…另一方面…
exercises.explanation: Balanced essays in Chinese almost always open with 凡事都有兩面 or a similar two-sides formula before laying out 一方面 / 另一方面.

lessons.title: Dialogue: Discussing a film at a coffee shop
lessons.description: Hedge your film opinions, half-agree, and recommend with a caveat

exercises.prompt: Coffee-shop chat about a film you saw last night

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: 你昨天看的那部電影怎麼樣？(Nǐ zuótiān kàn de nà bù diànyǐng zěnmeyàng?)
turns.spokenText: 你昨天看的那部電影怎麼樣？

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Soften your opinion (hedging).
options: 我覺得劇情比較拖沓，不過演技不錯。(Wǒ juéde jùqíng bǐjiào tuōtà, búguò yǎnjì búcuò.)
劇情絕對爛透了，沒什麼好說的。(Jùqíng juéduì làn tòule, méi shénme hǎo shuō de.)
電影雖然好，因此結尾差。(Diànyǐng suīrán hǎo, yīncǐ jiéwěi chà.)
turns.answer: 我覺得劇情比較拖沓，不過演技不錯。(Wǒ juéde jùqíng bǐjiào tuōtà, búguò yǎnjì búcuò.)

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: 對，我也覺得節奏有點慢。(Duì, wǒ yě juéde jiézòu yǒudiǎn màn.)
turns.spokenText: 對，我也覺得節奏有點慢。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Half-agree, then add a nuance.
options: 我部分同意，不過那些慢鏡頭反而很有味道。(Wǒ bùfèn tóngyì, búguò nàxiē màn jìngtóu fǎn'ér hěn yǒu wèidào.)
完全同意而且非常好。(Wánquán tóngyì érqiě fēicháng hǎo.)
不知道我無所謂的吧。(Bù zhīdào wǒ wúsuǒwèi de ba.)
turns.answer: 我部分同意，不過那些慢鏡頭反而很有味道。(Wǒ bùfèn tóngyì, búguò nàxiē màn jìngtóu fǎn'ér hěn yǒu wèidào.)

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: 說得也是。導演想表達的主題你看懂了嗎？(Shuō de yěshì. Dǎoyǎn xiǎng biǎodá de zhǔtí nǐ kàndǒng le ma?)
turns.spokenText: 說得也是。導演想表達的主題你看懂了嗎？

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Fill in the hedge — 'I feel maybe'.
turns.after: 是在講家庭的疏離感。(Wǒ ___ shì zài jiǎng jiātíng de shūlí gǎn.)
turns.answer: 覺得大概

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: 嗯，那種感覺確實貫穿全片。(Èn, nà zhǒng gǎnjué quèshí guànchuān quánpiàn.)
turns.spokenText: 嗯，那種感覺確實貫穿全片。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Recommend it — but with a caveat.
options: 推薦看，不過得有耐心，節奏比較慢。(Tuījiàn kàn, búguò děi yǒu nàixīn, jiézòu bǐjiào màn.)
強烈不推薦，肯定別看了。(Qiángliè bù tuījiàn, kěndìng bié kàn le.)
可以看也可以不看反正都行。(Kěyǐ kàn yě kěyǐ bù kàn fǎnzhèng dōu xíng.)
turns.answer: 推薦看，不過得有耐心，節奏比較慢。(Tuījiàn kàn, búguò děi yǒu nàixīn, jiézòu bǐjiào màn.)

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: 好，我下週找時間去看。(Hǎo, wǒ xià zhōu zhǎo shíjiān qù kàn.)
turns.spokenText: 好，我下週找時間去看。

topics.title: News & current events
topics.description: Read a headline, summarize what happened, give your take

lessons.title: News vocabulary
lessons.description: 新聞, 報道, 媒體 — the building blocks

exercises.prompt: the term to its meaning
What does "頭條新聞" (tóu tiáo xīn wén) mean?
exercises.explanation: 頭條 literally means "top entry" — but it's also the name of a hugely popular news app, 今日頭條.

exercises.prompt: "據報道" (jù bào dào) means ___
the news-vocabulary term
What does "自媒體" (zì méi tǐ) mean?
exercises.explanation: 自媒體 — literally "self-media". The Weibo / WeChat public accounts ecosystem; contrasted with 傳統媒體 (traditional media).

exercises.prompt: online vs traditional media term
Build "This piece of news got onto the trending list (熱搜)"
exercises.answer: 這 條 新聞 上 了 熱搜

exercises.prompt: "獨家報道" (dú jiā bào dào) means ___
What does "假新聞" (jiǎ xīn wén) mean?
Build "Today's headline news is about education reform"
exercises.answer: 今天 的 頭條 新聞 是 關於 教育 改革

exercises.prompt: Tap the news vocab you hear
exercises.spokenText: 突 發 新 聞
options: 突 發 新 聞
頭 條 新 聞
突 然 新 聞
熱 門 新 聞
exercises.answer: 突 發 新 聞
exercises.explanation: 突發 (tū fā) — "suddenly occurring" — pairs with 新聞 to form the breaking-news idiom. Don't confuse with 頭條 (headline) or 突然 (suddenly).

exercises.prompt: Which is the most NEWS-REGISTER way to start a sentence?
options: 我朋友說今天那個事兒…
exercises.explanation: 據相關媒體報道 — "according to relevant media reports" — the standard news opener. The casual options would never appear in a print or anchor segment.

lessons.title: What happened?
lessons.description: 發生, 引起, 影響 — narrating events

exercises.prompt: What does "發生" (fā shēng) mean?
Build "This event has had a big impact on society"
exercises.answer: 這件 事 對 社會 有 很大 的 影響

exercises.prompt: "引起廣泛關注" (yǐn qǐ guǎng fàn guān zhù) means ___
What does "事故" (shì gù) mean?
the verb to its meaning
Convert active to passive: "The accident was caused by drunk driving" using 被
exercises.answer: 這 起 事故 是 由 酒駕 造成 的
exercises.explanation: News register prefers 是…由…造成的 over plain 被. 由 marks the agent. 起 is the measure word for incidents.

exercises.prompt: Best translation for "This decision will have far-reaching effects":
options: 這個決定會產生深遠的影響
exercises.answer: 這個決定會產生深遠的影響
exercises.explanation: 產生影響 — "produce an impact" — is the standard collocation. 深遠 ("far-reaching") is essay-register.

exercises.prompt: "事件 (shì jiàn) 引發了 公眾 的 關注" means ___
acceptableAnswers: The incident set off public attention
exercises.explanation: 引發 = trigger / set off — slightly stronger and more news-y than 引起.

exercises.prompt: Build "The incident drew widespread attention from society"
exercises.answer: 這 件 事 引起 了 社會 的 廣泛 關注

exercises.prompt: Pick the news-headline-style passive: "The suspect was arrested":
exercises.explanation: Headlines use formal verbs: 逮捕 (arrest) over casual 抓. 警方 over casual 警察.

exercises.prompt: "目前已造成多人受傷" (mù qián yǐ zào chéng duō rén shòu shāng) means ___
exercises.answer: So far it has caused multiple injuries
acceptableAnswers: As of now, multiple people have been injured
Currently it has caused several people to be injured
exercises.explanation: 目前 (currently) is the news-register version of 現在. 已 (already) is its 已經 equivalent. Strip the casualness for an anchor's voice.

topics.title: Environment & climate
topics.description: Pollution, recycling, climate change — and the more you do, the more it helps

guide.intro: 越…越 (yuè…yuè) is one of the most useful patterns at B2 — and one of the prettiest. It means "the more X, the more Y". You'll hear it everywhere from weather reports to op-eds. This topic uses environmental issues as the playground for it.

sections.text: 越…越 — the more…the more
The pattern is fixed: 越 + verb/adjective, 越 + verb/adjective. The two halves can share a subject (which sits at the front) or have different subjects.

rows.pinyin: Tiān qì yuè lái yuè rè.
rows.translation: The weather is getting hotter and hotter.

rows.pinyin: Tā yuè shuō yuè shēng qì.
rows.translation: The more he talked, the angrier he got.
The rain came down heavier and heavier.

sections.text: 越來越 — getting X-er
越來越 (yuè lái yuè) is the most common form: "more and more". It always sits in front of an adjective or stative verb, and signals a trend over time.

rows.pinyin: Kōng qì yuè lái yuè chà.
rows.translation: The air is getting worse and worse.

rows.pinyin: Huán bǎo yuè lái yuè zhòng yào.
rows.translation: Environmental protection is getting more and more important.

sections.text: Don't add 很 between 越來越 and the adjective. "越來越很熱" is wrong — 越來越 already does the intensifying.
Two-subject form
When the two halves have different subjects, both subjects appear inside the pattern, after each 越:

rows.source: 天氣越冷，我越想吃火鍋。
rows.pinyin: Tiān qì yuè lěng, wǒ yuè xiǎng chī huǒ guō.
rows.translation: The colder the weather, the more I want hotpot.

exercises.prompt: "保護環境，人人有責" means ___

exercises.explanation: 環境保護 is the full formal noun. 環保 is the casual/spoken contraction. 保護環境 is the verb-object form.

lessons.title: The more, the more
lessons.description: Use 越…越 to describe trends

exercises.prompt: What does "天氣越來越熱" mean?
options: The weather is getting hotter and hotter
exercises.answer: The weather is getting hotter and hotter

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is GRAMMATICALLY WRONG?
exercises.explanation: 越來越 already intensifies — adding 很 is double-marking.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is GRAMMATICALLY WRONG?
exercises.explanation: Same rule: 越來越 cannot be paired with another intensifier like 非常 or 很. Drop the 非常 — 他越來越努力 is correct.

pairs.right: The more X, the more Y

exercises.explanation: 越來越 + adj is one of the most common B2 patterns spoken at conversational speed. Listen for the rising-falling cadence on 越來越.

exercises.answer: 我們應該多騎腳踏車，少開車
exercises.explanation: 多 + verb / 少 + verb is a clean way to recommend more/less of an action.

exercises.prompt: "節約用水" (jié yuē yòng shuǐ) means ___
Tap the sentence you hear
options: 今天 比 昨天 冷
今天 不 太 冷
exercises.explanation: 比較 (bǐ jiào, "relatively") and 比 (bǐ, "compared to") sound nearly identical — but 比 always needs a comparison object after it (比 X), while 比較 just modifies an adjective.

exercises.prompt: Build "Today is five degrees hotter than yesterday" (比 + numerical comparison)

exercises.explanation: 比 + numerical comparison: A 比 B + adj + amount. The amount goes AFTER the adjective: 高 五 釐米 (5 cm taller), 熱 五 度 (5 degrees hotter), 大 三 歲 (3 years older).

exercises.prompt: Best translation for "He is five centimeters taller than me":
exercises.explanation: Pattern: A 比 B + adjective + number/amount. The amount of difference always comes after the adjective.
